headline: GOLD SUFFERS LARGEST SINGLE-DAY DROP SINCE MARCH AS BLOWOUT JOBS REPORT KILLS RATE-CUT TRADE
snippet: Gold futures shed 3.3% to settle at $4,353.90 after US payrolls surged to 172,000 — nearly double the ~88,000 expected. Silver tumbled below $70, down over 7% for the week. CME FedWatch now shows 96% probability of a Fed hold; a year-end rate hike is being priced in. Gold has erased all 2026 gains.

headline: METALS FOCUS: GOLD MINE SUPPLY TO HIT ALL-TIME HIGH 3,907T IN 2026 — AVERAGE PRICE STILL SURGES 43% TO $4,920
snippet: Metals Focus forecasts record gold mine output of 3,907 tonnes in 2026, up 2.4% year-on-year, with all regions strengthening except Oceania and Europe. Despite softening demand and a growing market surplus, sustained geopolitical uncertainty supports a 2026 average gold price of $4,920 per ounce — up 43% from 2025.

headline: K92 MINING EXPANDS ARAKOMPA GOLD ZONE TO 300M DEPTH, 400M STRIKE — MAIDEN RESOURCE ESTIMATE DUE MID-2026
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNT) released its sixth batch of 33 drill holes from Arakompa, PNG — 100 holes drilled in total, every one of them mineralized. The AR1 high-grade zone now defined to 300m vertical depth and 400m strike length from 100m depth. Best intercept: 1.70m at 92.43 g/t AuEq. Maiden resource estimate targeted for mid-2026.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD HITS 3.24 G/T OVER 14.77M AT BIG MASTER SYSTEM; SECOND RIG LIFTS 2026 PROGRAM TO 45,000M
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSXV: DRY) released drill results from the Big Master Gold System at its Gold Rock project in Ontario. Hole DGR-051 returned 3.24 g/t Au over 14.77m, including a 29.55 g/t high-grade core over 1.35m. A second rig enters the program, lifting total 2026 planned meterage to 45,000m.

headline: MINING M&A ENTERS NEW PHASE: INVESTORS DEMAND GROWTH AND EXECUTION, NOT JUST CAPITAL ALLOCATION STORIES
snippet: Higher metals prices are handing miners more strategic options, but investors are growing less tolerant of complicated portfolios and missed guidance. Pan American Silver approved ~$146M for Phase 1 of its Timmins Camp Project. Adshead-Bell argues the deal cycle is shifting from announcement to delivery — and the market will punish those that don't deliver.

headline: ANGLO-TECK MEGA-MERGER DRAGS — FINAL REGULATORY APPROVAL NOW EXPECTED BETWEEN SEPTEMBER 2026 AND MARCH 2027
snippet: Anglo American's merger-of-equals with Teck Resources to create copper-focused Anglo Teck still awaits clearance from China and South Korea. Final approval is now expected between September 2026 and March 2027. The deal has already cleared Canada, Australia, and both shareholder votes. Copper integration synergies are the primary strategic driver.

headline: CHILE COPPER OUTPUT HITS NINE-YEAR LOW AS GRADE DECLINES AND WEATHER DISRUPTIONS PILE UP
snippet: Chile's copper production has slumped to a nine-year low as falling ore grades, adverse weather, and maintenance interruptions compound each other. Output has declined for seven consecutive rolling months. The supply weakness adds structural pressure to an already tight global copper market — even as prices pulled back 3.5% Friday on the Fed rate shock.

headline: GOLD SUMMER DOLDRUMS ARE HERE — HISTORY SAYS THIS IS THE WINDOW TO BUY BEFORE THE AUTUMN RALLY
snippet: GoldSeek's Adam Hamilton argues that gold's June weakness is the most predictable seasonal pattern in commodities — and the narrowest accumulation window of the year. Gold-futures speculators are at multi-year lows in positioning. With war-driven inflation poised to reignite and AI-stock bubble risk looming, the setup for gold's autumn rally looks intact.

headline: INFLATION'S COMEBACK: WHY THE FED MAY BE LOSING THE FIGHT AS OIL SHOCK MEETS RATE PARALYSIS
snippet: The Iran war oil shock is reigniting inflation just as the Fed is paralyzed between cutting rates to manage debt and hiking to control prices. Friday's blowout jobs print crystallized the dilemma. Analysis argues the Fed's credibility is eroding — a long-term positive for precious metals regardless of near-term volatility created by rate-hike repricing.
